Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Ben's note. Quick internal thoughts before we send a formal legal redline:

- Scope: limit carve-out to "grant-funded" or "scholarship" seats only; exclude promotional or institutional discounts.
- Duration: propose 12 months from effective date for the carve-out window; after that, counts toward committed floors.
- Cap: set a cap on carve-out volume (eg. 15% of total seats or N tokens) to protect economics.
- True-up: any seats outside the carve-out should be reconciled at the standard rate at the annual true-up; need guidance from Finance on revenue timing.

Attaching my redline suggestions (redline_suggestion.docx). I want to make the external language tight so we don't create an opening for broader exemptions.

Thanks — Priyom

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: EduPack pricing exhibit - internal note (proposed redline)

Priyom / Marissa — see inline suggested language below and attached plain-text redline (ExhibitB_EduException_redline.txt). I aimed for narrow, objective criteria to avoid open-ended carve-outs.

Proposed Exhibit B language (draft):
"Academic Grant and Scholarship Exception: For the avoidance of doubt, seats that are demonstrably funded through faculty research grants or student scholarship funds (each, a 'Grant Seat') shall be excluded from the calculation of Customer's minimum-commit usage floor for a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date, provided that: (a) Customer furnishes, within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date, a list of Grant Seats and associated purchase order numbers or cost-center codes; (b) Grant Seats do not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the aggregate committed seats for Year 1; and (c) Grant Seats are delineated on invoices using the cost-center code agreed in writing. Any Grant Seats exceeding the 15% cap will be included in minimum-commit calculations and subject to standard rates at true-up."

Notes / risk flags:
- Revenue recognition: Finance will need PO or cost-center tagging to defer revenue appropriately; if tagging is delayed we may not be able to exclude those seats in our books.
- Discounts: academic pricing may be applied to eligible customers per the order form; promotional discounts cannot be stacked with the academic discount unless explicitly stated. I recommend a one-line clause: "Promotional offers shall not stack with Academic Discounts unless expressly agreed in writing."

If you want, I can push this redline into the DocuSign envelope once Ben confirms the PO tagging approach.

Karthik Iyer
Lead, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ExhibitB_EduException_redline.txt (text)]
